title: LEQEMBI (lecanemab-irmb) Prescribing Information
one_line: The FDA prescribing information for LEQEMBI (lecanemab-irmb) outlines its indication for early Alzheimer's disease alongside severe boxed warnings regarding Amyloid Related Imaging Abnormalities (ARIA).
summary: This document is the official FDA-approved prescribing information for LEQEMBI (lecanemab-irmb), a monoclonal antibody directed against aggregated forms of beta amyloid. It is indicated for patients with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia associated with Alzheimer's disease. The label includes a prominent Boxed Warning for Amyloid Related Imaging Abnormalities (ARIA), including edema (ARIA-E) and hemosiderin deposition (ARIA-H), which can be severe and rarely fatal. Crucially, the label notes that ApoE ε4 homozygotes are at a significantly higher risk for ARIA and should be tested prior to treatment. Efficacy is supported by two clinical studies demonstrating significant reductions in brain amyloid beta plaque and a moderate slowing of clinical decline on the CDR-SB scale over 18 months. Strict guidelines for routine MRI monitoring and dose interruptions based on radiographic and clinical ARIA severity are mandated.

key_claims.claim: LEQEMBI reduces clinical decline on the global cognitive and functional scale compared to placebo.
key_claims.evidence: Study 2 showed an adjusted mean change from baseline at 18 months in CDR-SB of -0.45 (-27%) with p<0.0001.

key_claims.claim: LEQEMBI reduces amyloid beta plaque levels in the brain in a dose- and time-dependent manner.
key_claims.evidence: Study 1 showed a -0.310 SUVR difference from placebo (p<0.001) at Week 79; Study 2 showed continuous reductions from Week 13 through Week 79.

key_claims.claim: ApoE ε4 homozygotes have a markedly higher incidence of ARIA compared to heterozygotes and noncarriers.
key_claims.evidence: Study 2 incidence of ARIA was 45% in ApoE ε4 homozygotes vs 19% in heterozygotes and 13% in noncarriers. Severe radiographic ARIA-H was 13.5% in homozygotes vs 1.1% in noncarriers.

key_claims.claim: ApoE ε4 homozygotes did not show a treatment effect on the primary endpoint (CDR-SB).
key_claims.evidence: Exploratory subgroup analysis of ApoE ε4 homozygotes (15% of the trial population) showed no treatment effect on the primary endpoint, CDR-SB, compared to placebo.

methods.population: patients with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage of Alzheimer's disease and confirmed amyloid pathology
methods.duration: 18 months (79 weeks in Study 1; 18 months in Study 2)

funding_and_conflicts: Manufactured by Eisai Inc. and copyrighted by Eisai Inc. and Biogen. As a sponsor-authored FDA label, conflicts of interest are inherent.
limitations: Assays used to measure anti-lecanemab-irmb antibodies are subject to interference by serum lecanemab concentrations, potentially underestimating the incidence of neutralizing antibody formation.
Exploratory subgroup analysis of ApoE ε4 homozygotes showed no primary treatment effect, limiting confidence in efficacy for the highest-risk subgroup.
red_flags: ApoE ε4 homozygotes represent a subpopulation that faces roughly double the risk of ARIA (45%) and a vastly higher risk of severe microhemorrhages (13.5%), yet the exploratory analysis states that a treatment effect was not observed on the primary clinical endpoint (CDR-SB) for this exact group.
Patients taking LEQEMBI with an anticoagulant had an intracerebral hemorrhage incidence of 2.5% compared to none on placebo, highlighting severe bleeding risks with standard comorbidities.
